entry.title: zip: Critical Parser Differential & Security Control Bypass via Dual-Header Inconsistencies (Zip Cloaking) Leading to Arbitrary File Overwrite & RCE (CVE-2026-115905)
entry.content:
vulnerability · parser-differential · CVE-2026-115905

The Rust `zip` crate (versions ≤9.0.4) contains a critical parser differential vulnerability (CVE-2026-115905) where `ZipArchive` and `ZipStreamReader` interpret filenames differently—the former trusts the Central Directory File Header while the latter relies on the Local File Header. Attackers can craft malicious ZIP archives with inconsistent headers to achieve arbitrary file overwrites and remote code execution, exploiting this inconsistency to bypass security controls. This vulnerability is critical severity; no active exploitation in the wild has been confirmed at time of advisory. Immediately update to `zip` version >9.0.4 and validate all ZIP extraction logic, particularly any code using `ZipStreamReader`.

This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild and can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to achieve remote code execution as root, including PHP webshell implantation. Immediately apply kernel security updates per vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 prioritization guidance; affected systems should be patched without delay given active exploitation. If patches are unavailable, discontinue use of the affected kernel versions and perform forensic triage per CISA requirements.

This vulnerability has high severity and is exploited in the wild; it requires network-level access and affects systems configured for network booting. Hardware vendors using EDK II must immediately patch affected UEFI implementations, and organizations should disable network boot by default, restrict PXE boot access to trusted networks only, and validate boot images cryptographically where possible.

This is exploited in the wild and affects all applications using Authlib's JWS JSON deserialization. Upgrade immediately to Authlib 1.9.0 or later to patch this critical vulnerability.

This is actively exploitable and affects any Echo application using the Proxy middleware with route-level security controls. Users should immediately upgrade to patched versions of echo/v4 and echo/v5 and review any proxied traffic for potential unauthorized access.

Update Wasmtime to v43 or later immediately, which remediates the issue by using full u32 indices instead of bit-packed values. No evidence of wild exploitation currently reported, but the critical severity and sandbox escape potential warrant emergency patching.

Cisco Secure Email Gateway is affected by CVE-2026-76519, a relative path traversal vulnerability enabling unauthenticated remote attackers to write arbitrary files to the underlying operating system. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild and carries high severity due to the lack of authentication requirements and potential for complete system compromise. Immediately apply vendor mitigations per CISA BOD 26-04 guidelines; if mitigations are unavailable, discontinue use of the product. Conduct forensics triage on potentially compromised systems and assess internet exposure of all affected assets.

entry.title: Hackers Backdoor Nextcloud Servers Through Critical Flaw in Collabora’s Built-in CODE App
entry.content:
vulnerability · rce · CVE-2026-110447

A critical vulnerability in Nextcloud's optional Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server app allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code and plant web shells on affected servers. The flaw has been actively exploited in the wild since at least September 10, with documented cases affecting multiple Nextcloud installations. Administrators should immediately update the Collabora Online app to the patched version and review server logs for suspicious activity or unauthorized web shell uploads. Alternatively, disable or remove the Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server app if the functionality is not required.

entry.title: Cisco Warns of Active Attacks Exploiting New Critical Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability
entry.content:
vulnerability · rce

Cisco Secure Email Gateway contains a critical unauthenticated file write vulnerability (CVE-2024-20421) that allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root by sending crafted email attachments. This flaw is actively exploited in the wild with no authentication required. Immediate patching is essential; organizations should apply Cisco's available security updates or implement temporary workarounds if patches cannot be deployed immediately.

entry.title: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host
entry.content:
vulnerability · privilege-escalation · CVE-2026-74580, CVE-2026-99999

CVE-2026-74580 affects the Linux kernel's vhost subsystem across multiple versions spanning approximately a decade. The vulnerability allows local users to read and write arbitrary kernel memory, escalate to root privileges, and in virtualization scenarios enables guest VMs to access host memory and compromise the hypervisor process. Severity is critical with active exploitation potential in multi-tenant cloud environments. Immediate kernel patching is required; users should prioritize updates for affected distributions and review VM isolation controls pending patch deployment.

entry.title: An AI Agent Found a Critical OTP Bypass in Production. The Attack Was the Easy Part.
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass

An AI pentesting agent identified a critical authentication bypass in a major insurer's production login system where users could arbitrarily redirect one-time passcodes to attacker-controlled destinations, circumventing OTP-based multi-factor authentication. This vulnerability allows complete account takeover with minimal technical sophistication and represents a fundamental flaw in OTP delivery validation rather than a weak implementation. The severity is critical with high exploitability; while discovered during authorized testing, the simplicity of the attack suggests it could be weaponized in the wild if not remediated. The affected organization must immediately implement server-side validation restricting OTP delivery destinations to pre-registered user-controlled channels, audit logs for exploitation evidence, and enforce strict controls over OTP transmission parameters.

Read more · Source: thehackernews

entry.title: Hirudo Android Trojan Uses Patched Banking Apps to Bypass Their Built-In Security Checks
entry.content:
red-team · banking-fraud

Hirudo is an Android banking trojan that replaces legitimate banking apps with modified versions that disable built-in security checks, targeting Indonesian financial institutions. The malware operates by sideloading patched banking apps that bypass security mechanisms from within the application itself, representing an escalation in mobile banking fraud techniques. This represents a high-severity threat with active exploitation in the wild targeting Indonesian users. Users should uninstall suspicious banking apps, download only from official app stores, and enable Google Play Protect; financial institutions should enhance device attestation and implement server-side anomaly detection to identify compromised client instances.

Read more · Source: thehackernews

entry.title: Researchers Used a Public OpenAI Model to Build a $250,000 Chrome Full-Chain Exploit in Six Days
entry.content:
vulnerability · rce

Researchers used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model to chain three previously unknown Google Chrome vulnerabilities into a full exploit capable of arbitrary code execution on Windows via malicious web pages, demonstrating AI-assisted vulnerability discovery at scale. The exploit achieved high severity (full system compromise) and was not exploited in the wild before disclosure. Google has patched all three vulnerabilities and awarded XBOW a maximum bug bounty; organizations should apply Chrome updates immediately and consider restricting AI model access to security researchers given the accelerated exploit development timeline.

entry.title: curl Patches HTTP/2 Upload Flaw After PoC Demonstrates Client-Side Code Execution
entry.content:
vulnerability · memory-corruption

curl versions prior to 8.23.0 contain an HTTP/2 upload vulnerability allowing malicious servers to corrupt client memory during file uploads, potentially enabling code execution. The flaw requires precise knowledge of the victim's build and memory layout, and exploitation typically results in client crashes, limiting practical real-world impact. A proof-of-concept has been publicly demonstrated. Affected organizations should upgrade to curl 8.23.0 or later immediately, particularly systems performing uploads to untrusted servers.

entry.title: Ghostscript flaw lets hackers hijack servers via PDF uploads
entry.content:
vulnerability · heap-buffer-overflow · CVE-2026-112900, CVE-2026-39919

Ghostscript PDF interpreter contains a critical heap buffer overflow (CVE-2026-39919) enabling remote code execution via malicious PDF uploads. The vulnerability affects file upload functionality across web services and document processing systems that use Ghostscript for rendering. No active exploitation in the wild has been confirmed at this time, though the critical severity rating and ease of weaponization via PDF attachments present significant risk. Apply available security patches immediately and implement input validation on PDF uploads as a compensating control until patching is complete.

entry.content:
vulnerability · mixed

entry.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-70188 - ASP.NET Core Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
entry.content:
vulnerability · security-feature-bypass · CVE-2026-70188

CVE-2026-70188 affects Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core across multiple platforms (Linux ARM/x64, macOS). The vulnerability is a security feature bypass where Kestrel improperly accepts newline characters in HTTP/2 request trailers and HPACK dynamic table values instead of rejecting them as malformed, potentially allowing request smuggling or header injection attacks. Severity is critical with no indication of current wild exploitation. Developers must update the affected Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime packages to patched versions immediately.

entry.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-88092 - ASP.NET Core Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
entry.content:
vulnerability · request-smuggling · CVE-2026-88092

Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core contains a critical HTTP request smuggling vulnerability (CVE-2026-88092) where aborted HTTP/1 connections can reparse unread request-body bytes as separate requests, enabling request desynchronization attacks. The vulnerability affects multiple runtime packages across Linux and macOS platforms and is classified as critical severity. Immediate patching is required; developers must update to the latest patched version of Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime packages across all affected platform variants. Monitor for exploitation attempts targeting Kestrel-based applications until patches are fully deployed.

entry.title: Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass

Docker Hub contained a critical authorization flaw in the account-to-organization conversion feature that persisted for two years, allowing authenticated users to push, pull, or delete container images as another user. The vulnerability affected Docker Hub's core image registry functionality and had CVSS severity indicating critical risk. Docker reports no evidence of active exploitation in the wild. Affected users should ensure their Docker Hub installation is updated to the patched version released September 30, 2024, and review image repository access logs for unauthorized activity.

entry.title: Releasing the Cobalt Strike Beacon Corpus
entry.content:
red-team · c2

Fox-IT released a comprehensive dataset of 56,843 Cobalt Strike Beacon samples with parsed configurations collected from over 30,600 unique command-and-control servers between July 2018 and September 2026. This corpus documents widespread exploitation of Cobalt Strike, a legitimate penetration testing framework frequently weaponized by threat actors for post-exploitation activities. The dataset provides security researchers and defenders with detailed intelligence on malicious beacon infrastructure, configurations, and deployment patterns to improve detection and attribution capabilities. Organizations should use this corpus to enhance threat hunting, update detection signatures for Cobalt Strike C2 communication patterns, and conduct forensic analysis of compromised systems potentially connected to these known malicious Team Servers.
